newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Defence chiefs to defuse tension in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Defence chiefs to defuse tension in Cambodia.

text.p: Cambodia's two main coalition parties have agreed to pull back their forces in northwestern Battambang province where clashes this week left dead on both sides, royalist leader Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Friday.

Co-Defence Ministers Tea Banh of the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) and Tea Chamrath of the royalist FUNCINPEC party were to fly to the rice-bowl province later on Friday to try to defuse tension, added First Prime Minister Ranariddh.

"I have suggested to withdraw all of the forces (of the rival parties) back to the previous positions and after that let us resolve the remaining problem," Ranariddh told reporters at a ground-breaking ceremony for a new airport terminal.
Ranariddh said Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of the CPP had been given his proposals on Thursday evening and "Hun Sen has accepted my proposal".

FUNCINPEC and CPP troops have clashed this week in Battambang's Moung district, sources from both sides said. The fighting was linked to Khmer Rouge defectors, with some of the former guerrillas siding with the CPP and some with FUNCINPEC.

Human rights workers in Battambang said on Friday they had reports that 14 CPP and two FUNCINPEC soldiers were killed over the past three days, and that 19 CPP soldiers had been wounded in fighting around Thippadei mountain and in Battambang city.

Rival premiers Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run elections in 1993, had been expected to discuss the problems in Battambang and a draft electoral law during a cabinet meeting on Friday.
But Ranariddh said the meeting had been postponed at the request of Hun Sen, who also missed the airport ceremony and travelled instead to open a school in an eastern province.
